title: Rollout tempering: traffic lattice config and guardrail interpreter
creator: Aparna Rao
description: Implement a flexible, expressive configuration and policy interpreter for canary rollouts that we call the 'traffic lattice'. The lattice must support time-based step schedules, metric-based gate checks, weighted traffic splits including multi-variant A/B, shadow (mirrored) traffic, and deterministic auto-rollback rules. This ticket covers the configuration schema, guardrail interpreter, and a small runtime shim to evaluate policies at decision points. It does NOT include rollout UI changes in Console (separate PM ticket) nor the full canary orchestration loop integration (follow-up task).
acceptance_criteria: A human-readable JSON/YAML schema (v1) exists for traffic lattice configs and validates with a schema validator
Runtime interpreter evaluates step schedules and returns a deterministic traffic split and control actions within 50ms p95 for a typical config
Guardrails support threshold-based and statistical checks (error-rate, p99 latency, quality-regression via eval hooks) and can emit PASS/FAIL/DEFER
Auto-rollback can be configured with min-observation windows and will produce an action log entry that the orchestrator can consume
Unit tests and integration harness (simulated traffic) cover at least 90% of new interpreter code paths
Documentation and example configs for: simple ramp, A/B experiment, shadowing, and auto-rollback scenarios
implementation_notes: Design a compact declarative schema: steps[] with duration/traffic/conditions, policies{} for guardrails, and hooks[] for evals or external checks
Interpreter will be library-only (go) with a thin HTTP shim for local testing; keep surface area stable for Console integration
Use existing metrics API from observability layer; interpret metric expressions as: namespace.metric{filters}.agg over window
Statistical checks: implement A/B uplift calculator (Wilson score / bootstrap) for quality regression detection; default to conservative thresholds
Fallback behavior: if metrics backend is unavailable, interpreter returns DEFER and the orchestrator should keep current traffic or fallback to safe model variant
Config validation must surface clear human-friendly errors referencing line numbers (when YAML) and schema ids

rollout_sample_config:
# YAML example (v1)
version: v1
name: progressive-tempering-demo
steps:
  - name: step-1
    duration: 10m
    traffic: {model-v2: 5%, model-v1: 95%}
    conditions:
      - type: metric_threshold
        metric: infra.error_rate{model=model-v2}.p99
        operator: lt
        value: 0.02
  - name: step-2
    duration: 30m
    traffic: {model-v2: 30%, model-v1: 70%}
    conditions:
      - type: ab_quality_check
        metric: eval.accuracy{prompt_set=smoke}.uplift
        operator: gte
        value: 0.01
policies:
  auto_rollback:
    enabled: true
    min_window: 5m
    failure_thresholds:
      error_rate: 0.05
      latency_p99: 1000ms
  shadowing:
    enabled: true
    mirror_percentage: 100%
risk_mitigation: Conservative defaults: all new configs start with 0% traffic unless explicitly set
Require an explicit 'safety' approval label for any rollout where model-v2 traffic > 30% in the first 24h
Add telemetry to detect interpreter-decision divergence vs orchestrator-execution and alert immediately
Provide manual kill switch for customer-facing rollouts; orchestrator must respect operator fastest-path to rollback
testing_plan: Unit tests for schema validation and guardrail evaluation (edge cases including missing metrics)
Integration test with ops-sim to replay historic traffic and assert rollback triggers on injected regressions
Load test for interpreter with 500 concurrent decision evaluations to verify p95 latency under load
E2E demo using a canary with shadow traffic and an artificial evaluation hook (QA harness)
notes: Trade-offs: we intentionally keep interpreter conservative to reduce false positives on rollback; this may slow legitimate rollouts.
Decision: bootstrap-based A/B test will be default for quality checks; param tunables will be exposed in v2 of schema.
Follow-ups: Console preview UI, orchestrator binding glue, and a customer-facing runbook for manual rollback.
